free_tier.stated: VPS - NAT512 at USD 7.50/year: 512 MB RAM, 5 GB SSD, 1 CPU core (fair use), a /80 IPv6 plus a shared NAT IPv4 with 20 usable ports and 1 SSH port, 750 GB transfer per month. The second plan, VPS - NAT768, is USD 10/year with 768 MB, 7 GB SSD and 1024 GB transfer per month. Locations listed on the vendor page: Los Angeles, New York, Canada, Netherlands, France, Norway, Japan, Singapore. The tracker row adds a 1 Gbps port and the same USD 0.63/month equivalent.

egress.terms: 750 GB transfer per month included on NAT512 and 1024 GB on NAT768, both vendor-stated; nothing is published about what happens past the allowance

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: SSH with root; the vendor states the VPS are 'fully unmanaged' and support is limited to service functionality; no API was mentioned on the page read. IPv4 reach is by NAT port forwarding, 20 usable ports plus 1 SSH port.
chaining: At USD 7.50 a year this is the cheapest IPv4-reachable always-on box: a DNS resolver, an uptime probe, a cron runner, a WireGuard endpoint, or an IPv6-only crawler front end behind Cloudflare as the vendor's own use-case list suggests. It cannot be a general crawler egress host, because 20 forwarded ports and 750 GB a month cap both the connection count and the bytes.

limits.value: 750 GB transfer a month is the vendor's own figure for NAT512 and is the first limit a daytime fetcher meets, at about 25 GB a day. The second limit is address surface: a shared NAT IPv4 with 20 forwarded ports cannot hold many parallel TLS connections.
